name: Old Town
vibe: Kala and Abanotubani — the sulphur baths, the crooked balconies and the fortress above them

name: Sololaki
vibe: Art-nouveau stairwells, painted hallways and courtyard cafés on the hill behind Freedom Square

name: Mtatsminda
vibe: The funicular, the pantheon and the park on the ridge — the whole city from above

name: Avlabari
vibe: The cathedral hill on the left bank, Armenian Tbilisi, and the cable car down to the river

name: Vera
vibe: Quiet streets between Rustaveli and Vake — the cafés, the bakeries, the neighbourhood people move to

name: Vake
vibe: The park, the embassies and Chavchavadze Avenue — Tbilisi's polished side

name: Marjanishvili
vibe: The left bank's theatre square, Fabrika's courtyard, Aghmashenebeli's cafés — the newest energy in the city

name: Saburtalo
vibe: Big, busy, residential — universities, metro stops and the best-value flats in the centre's reach

name: Isani
vibe: Left-bank residential along the metro's first line — local prices, ten minutes from the Old Town

name: Didube
vibe: The marshrutka station for the whole country, the big markets, and the trains north

name: Dighomi
vibe: New builds and family blocks on the way out of town — quiet, cheaper, car-friendly

name: Gldani
vibe: The Soviet microdistricts at the end of the metro — the most local end of Tbilisi

name: Kojori
vibe: The pine plateau above the city — summer air, forest walks and Turtle Lake on the way

name: Mtskheta
vibe: The old capital half an hour away — Jvari on its hill, Svetitskhoveli below, UNESCO on both

name: Sighnaghi
vibe: Kakheti's wine town on a ridge — cellars, the Alazani valley and the Caucasus wall behind it

name: Gudauri
vibe: The ski resort on the Georgian Military Highway — two hours up, snow from December

name: Stepantsminda
vibe: Kazbegi — the Gergeti church under a 5,000-metre peak, the day trip everyone does once
